non_bechina_section_analysis.paragraph: Sentence 1 — the teaching about חֲלִיף טוֹב (a good exchange/knife) and the vessels of the Beit HaMikdash
non_bechina_section_analysis.explanation: The first paragraph states that through חֲלִיף טוֹב one can see the faces of the כֵּלִים שֶׁל בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ (Temple vessels). It grounds this in Isaac's command to Esau 'שָׂא נָא כֵלֶיךָ' (Genesis 27:3) and the Midrash (Bereshit Rabbah 65) which interprets 'כֵלֶיךָ' as an allusion to the Temple vessels (specifically Babylon's taking of them). The verbs throughout are 'רָמַז' (hinted/alluded) and 'מְרַמֵּז' (alludes). This is homiletic exegesis (derash/remez), not the bechina identity claim ('X הוּא בְחִינַת Y'). The connection between חֲלִיף טוֹב, סַּכִּין, and כֵּלִים שֶׁל בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ is one of allusion and spiritual correspondence (seeing/perceiving), not shared essential nature. Therefore these concepts cannot and should not be encoded as bechina nodes for Torah #278.
non_bechina_section_analysis.verdict: None of these concepts use bechina language. They should not be added to the bechina dataset for Torah #278.
